direction: Perform large cluster excision and joint reinsertion instead of replacing one or two points. Choose a seed point with high contact degree, remove a connected cluster of $8$, $12$, or $16$ points consisting of the seed and its closest angular/contact neighbours, freeze the remaining points, and re-optimize all removed points simultaneously—including their interactions with one another—using batched annealed LogSumExp Adam from at least 32 random initializations inside the cavity. Rank the resulting completions by exact max cosine and by distance from the original cluster, unfreeze and refine only the best three to five, and then run a short LP polish; this creates a genuinely different local contact topology because no single reinserted point is forced back into its old socket, while the untouched majority preserves most of the record's quality.

idea: Hinge feasibility search below the record with L-BFGS on normalized variables plus LP polish.
direction: Replace minimization of the maximum by a below-record feasibility search. For target thresholds $t=0.2439,0.2437,0.2435,0.2432$, minimize the analytic hinge objective $\sum_{i<j}\max(0,\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-t)^2$, optionally plus a much smaller hinge at $t-0.005$ to control near-violations, using L-BFGS on normalized variables from the record perturbed by tangent noise of sizes $0.01$, $0.03$, and $0.08$. Because non-violating pairs exert no force, this permits large rearrangements of the hundreds of presently tied pairs instead of asking every contact to improve simultaneously; whenever the violating-pair count reaches zero, record that configuration, lower $t$, and continue. Allocate the time budget over several targets and perturbations, finish with LP polish on the feasible or least-violating distinct candidate, and always return the best exact max-cosine configuration found rather than the final iterate.

idea: Optimize 47 antipodal representatives for the projective max-absolute-cosine objective from greedy-antipode and random starts, then break symmetry with tangent shakes and refine the full 94 with annealed LogSumExp plus LP polish.
direction: Search first in an antipodally symmetric low-dimensional ansatz, then deliberately break the symmetry. Construct 47 pairs $\{\pm y_k\}$ by optimizing only the 47 representatives with the projective objective of minimizing the maximum of $|\langle y_k,y_\ell\rangle|$ for $k<\ell$, initialized both randomly and by greedily pairing each record vector with the vector closest to its antipode and projecting those pairs onto exact antipodes. Anneal a smooth approximation to this absolute-value minimax objective, then release all 94 points independently with small random tangent perturbations of several magnitudes and continue with the below-record hinge objective and LP polish; the symmetric stage explores a qualitatively different, highly coordinated family, while symmetry breaking can only enlarge the feasible set and may descend below the unstructured record basin.

idea: Curvature-corrected active-set SQP polish with 1e-6 active set in per-point tangent coordinates, LP minimax subproblem plus exact renormalization with backtracking and rank-tested null-space equalization of the near-contact plateau.
direction: Build a curvature-corrected active-set SQP polish for the current basin: define active pairs by slack below $10^{-6}$ rather than $10^{-9}$, parameterize displacements in an orthonormal basis for each point's 12-dimensional tangent space, solve the linearized minimax QP with `scipy.optimize.lsq_linear`/an LP subproblem, then apply exact renormalization and a second-order correction plus backtracking line search on the true maximum. Iterate with trust radii $10^{-3},3\times10^{-4},10^{-4},\ldots$ while retaining all pairs whose slack falls below ten times the trial step, and explicitly test whether the active-contact Jacobian is rank-deficient; use null-space moves to equalize the hundreds of near-contacts instead of letting the LP radius collapse. Run this for at most 60 seconds, keep it only if it beats `best.npy`, and otherwise return the incumbent.

idea: Symmetry-constrained cyclic-shift search with LogSumExp L-BFGS on orbit representatives followed by symmetry breaking and unrestricted polish.
direction: Search symmetry-constrained algebraic constructions before unrestricted polishing: generate codes from a few orbit representatives under coordinate permutations and sign changes in $\mathbb{R}^{13}$, including orbit-size combinations summing to 94 such as $26+26+26+16$, $26+26+13+13+16$, and unions involving coordinate axes or cross-polytopal points, then optimize only the representatives' coordinates with L-BFGS on a LogSumExp objective. Randomly initialize at least 100 representative sets with different orbit partitions, score the expanded 94-point codes exactly, retain the five lowest, break symmetry with tangent perturbations of sizes $0.005$, $0.02$, and $0.05$, and finish each with unrestricted Adam plus LP polish. This targets the balanced, repeatable contact patterns absent from the current unstructured point cloud while still guaranteeing a valid $94\times13$ output.

idea: Build 7 thirteen-cycles plus 3 free points with unsigned/signed/antipodal variants, optimize only orbit representatives with averaged LogSumExp Adam, then break symmetry with quantile crushing and LP polish.
direction: Search a structured symmetric family completely away from the record basin, then break the symmetry: exploit $13$ being prime by building configurations from orbits of a 13-cycle coordinate permutation—seven orbits of 13 points (91 total) generated from seven representative unit vectors, plus three points fixed as a small optimised set on the cycle-invariant subspace to reach 94. Optimise only the representatives (averaging gradients over each orbit so symmetry is preserved exactly) with LogSumExp Adam at several random initialisations and orbit sign/permutation variants, evaluate the symmetric optimum, and then release all 94 points for quantile top-600 crushing and LP polishing; also try the analogous construction with a signed 13-cycle and with one 13-orbit replaced by antipodal representatives. Keep each symmetric construction under 30 s, compare against the incumbent only after symmetry-breaking polish, enforce the 165 s total deadline, and return the best valid array encountered.

idea: Broad-plateau equalizing annealed LogSumExp Adam with mean-penalty plus worst-point basin-hopping and final trust-region LP polish to build a jammed contact network.
Diverse annealed parents plus Procrustes-aligned slerp crossover with quantile-crush and LP polishing.
direction: Create genuinely different basins and recombine them by Procrustes crossover rather than polishing one parent: generate a pool of 10--14 diverse parents by jittering `best.npy` with $\sigma\in\{0.15,0.3,0.5,0.8\}$ plus two fully random starts, giving each only a short annealed LogSumExp Adam run (about 400 steps, $k:30\to300$) so they remain distinct, and retain the best few by maximum cosine. For each pair of parents, align them by alternating Hungarian matching on pairwise inner products with orthogonal Procrustes rotation, form children by per-matched-point slerp interpolation at $\alpha\in\{0.3,0.5,0.7\}$ (plus small $0.03$ jitter), renormalise, then polish children with a top-600 quantile-crush phase followed by at most 20 s of LP polishing; keep an elite archive, use children only if they beat their worse parent, and iterate recombination among elites until 165 s, returning the global best and never discarding the original incumbent.

idea: Contact-forming tangent LP continuation at the native 1e-7 scale with tightening active thresholds and tie-count guarded acceptance.
direction: Build a contact-forming continuation that works at the native $10^{-7}$ scale instead of the misleading $10^{-9}$ scale: load `best.npy`, compute all pair slacks, form an active set from slack $<3\times10^{-7}$ (capped at the tightest 2000 pairs), and repeatedly solve the sparse tangent-space LP (94$\times$12 displacement variables plus $t$, scipy `linprog`/HiGHS) with trust radius starting at $3\times10^{-4}$, exact renormalisation and backtracking over $\alpha\in\{1,\tfrac12,\tfrac14,\dots\}$. After each accepted step, tighten the active threshold geometrically $10^{-6}\to10^{-7}\to10^{-8}\to10^{-9}\to10^{-10}$ and continue, explicitly tracking as success metrics not only the maximum but the number of pairs with slack $<10^{-10}$ and the minimum contacts per point; accept moves that reduce the maximum without reducing this emerging tie count, and restart the radius at $10^{-4}$ whenever tightening creates at least 50 new near-ties. Keep the best configuration ever evaluated, enforce a hard 165 s deadline, and fall back to the incumbent on any solver failure.

idea: Delete-and-reinsert plateau hubs with 4096-candidate scoring, fixed-others LogSumExp Adam and short LP polish.
direction: Use discrete delete-and-reinsert topology changes focused on the plateau hubs: compute near-contact degrees at slack $<10^{-6}$, rank points by (a) membership in the top pair, (b) number of pairs within $10^{-7}$ of the maximum, and (c) sum of exponentials $\sum_j e^{(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-m)/10^{-7}}$, then repeatedly remove one hub point—or occasionally two points joined by a near-maximal pair—and optimally reinsert it against the fixed remaining 93 points. For reinsertion, score 4096 cheap candidates (random sphere samples, antipodes and normalised differences of its former neighbours, and perturbations of its old position), take the best 16 by true maximum cosine to the fixed set, refine only those with 200 steps of fixed-others LogSumExp Adam, then run a short 5 s LP polish of the full configuration; accept strictly improving reinsertions and otherwise restore the incumbent, cycling through hub choices until the 165 s deadline, always returning the best full (94,13) array found.

direction: Use discrete delete-and-reinsert topology changes focused on the plateau hubs: compute near-contact degrees at slack $<10^{-6}$, rank points by (a) membership in the top pair, (b) number of pairs within $10^{-7}$ of the maximum, and (c) sum of exponentials $\sum_j e^{(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-m)/10^{-7}}$, then repeatedly remove one hub point—or occasionally two points joined by a near-maximal pair—and optimally reinsert it against the fixed remaining 93 points. For reinsertion, score 4096 cheap candidates (random sphere samples, antipodes and normalised differences of its former neighbours, and perturbations of its old position), take the best 16 by true maximum cosine to the fixed set, refine only those with 200 steps of fixed-others LogSumExp Adam, then run a short 5 s LP polish of the full configuration; accept strictly improving reinsertions and otherwise restore the incumbent, cycling through hub choices until the 165 s deadline, always returning the best full (94,13) array found.
